author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Vic Mellor won the Republican nomination in Rhode Island’s 2nd Congressional District on Wednesday, defeating party-endorsed candidate Stephen Skoly, NBC 10 News reported.

The result advances Mellor to the November 3 general election against Democratic Rep. Seth Magaziner, who represents the district. NBC 10 reported the outcome after the primary but did not include a final certified vote total in its article; state election officials will complete the canvass before certifying results.

Mellor campaigned as a supporter of President Donald Trump and described his platform as putting Rhode Island interests first. Skoly, an oral surgeon, had emphasized opposition to government mandates and received the state party’s endorsement. The campaign presented Republican voters with differing backgrounds and approaches to challenging an incumbent.

Rhode Island’s 2nd District covers the western and southern portions of the state and includes part of Providence County. The fall contest now moves from an intraparty primary to a general-election comparison between Mellor and Magaziner. Neither party’s nomination should be treated as the final election result before November voting.
dek: Mellor defeated party-endorsed candidate Stephen Skoly and will face Democratic incumbent Seth Magaziner in the November 3 election.
headline: Vic Mellor wins Rhode Island 2nd District Republican primary
